name: commerce_set2_p1
label: Commerce: set 2 (foreign trade, documents and the aids to trade)

papers.title: Foreign Trade: practice set 1
papers.description: 8 original WASSCE-style objective questions on foreign trade, each with a worked solution and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: Importing goods and re-exporting them to another country with little or no processing is
questions.explanation:
Entrepôt (re-export) trade: goods are imported first, then re-exported.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- export trade: Export trade sells home-produced goods abroad.
- home trade: Home trade takes place within one country.
- wholesale trade: Wholesale trade is buying in bulk and selling to retailers.

questions.stem: Which is a difference between home trade and foreign trade?
questions.explanation:
Foreign trade needs foreign exchange; home trade uses one currency.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- Home trade needs a bill of lading: Bills of lading are used mainly in foreign trade by sea.
- Home trade pays import duties: Import duties apply to foreign trade.
- Foreign trade has lower transport costs: Foreign trade usually has higher transport costs.

options.label: B
options.content: Home trade needs a bill of lading

options.label: D
options.content: Foreign trade has lower transport costs

questions.stem: A country's visible exports are worth NLe 9,000 million and its visible imports NLe 13,000 million. What is its balance of trade (NLe million)?
questions.explanation:
Balance of trade = visible exports − visible imports = 9,000 − 13,000 = −4,000: an unfavourable balance.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 4,000: You subtracted exports from imports; the balance is exports minus imports.
- 22,000: You added exports and imports.
- -6,000: That includes invisible trade; the balance of trade covers goods only.

questions.stem: The index of export prices is 110 and the index of import prices is 125. What are the terms of trade?
questions.explanation:
Terms of trade $= \dfrac{110}{125} \times 100 = 88$: unfavourable, because it is below 100.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 113.6: You divided import prices by export prices.
- -15: You subtracted the indices instead of dividing them.
- 235: You added the two indices.

questions.stem: Shipping, insurance, banking and tourism services sold abroad are
questions.explanation:
Invisible trade is trade in services; visible trade is trade in goods.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- visible exports: Visible exports are goods.
- visible imports: These services are sold abroad, so they are exports.
- entrepôt goods: Entrepôt trade is in goods.

questions.stem: A complete ban on trade in a good or with a country is
questions.explanation:
An embargo stops trade completely, often for political, health or security reasons.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- a quota: A quota limits the quantity; it does not ban it completely.
- a tariff: A tariff is a tax on imports or exports.
- a subsidy: A subsidy is government help to local producers.

questions.stem: A main reason for protecting infant industries is to
questions.explanation:
Young firms with high costs are shielded from foreign competition for a time.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- increase the variety of imported goods: Protection reduces imports.
- lower prices for consumers immediately: Protection usually raises prices.
- encourage smuggling: Smuggling is a harmful side effect, not a reason.

options.label: A
options.content: increase the variety of imported goods

options.label: C
options.content: allow new local industries to grow until they can compete

questions.stem: In Sierra Leone, import duties are collected by the customs services of the
questions.explanation:
The NRA's customs services collect duties, check documents and prevent smuggling.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- Bank of Sierra Leone: The central bank manages money and banks, not customs.
- Sierra Leone Ports and Harbours Authority: The ports authority runs the ports; customs collect duties.
- Sierra Leone Standards Bureau: The Standards Bureau sets and tests product standards.

options.label: C
options.content: Sierra Leone Ports and Harbours Authority

papers.topic: Documents and Terms in Foreign Trade
papers.title: Documents and Terms in Foreign Trade: practice set 1
papers.description: 8 original WASSCE-style objective questions on documents and terms in foreign trade, each with a worked solution and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: The document a seller sends to correct an overcharge on an invoice is a
questions.explanation:
A credit note reduces the amount the buyer owes: overcharges, returns or damaged goods.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- debit note: A debit note corrects an undercharge, so the buyer owes more.
- statement of account: A statement summarises transactions and the balance owed.
- delivery note: A delivery note goes with the goods.

questions.stem: A pro forma invoice is sent
questions.explanation:
It shows what the invoice will be and supports advance payment or an import licence application.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- after payment, as proof of payment: Proof of payment is a receipt.
- to correct an undercharge: That is a debit note.
- at the end of the month to summarise transactions: That is a statement of account.

options.label: A
options.content: after payment, as proof of payment

options.label: C
options.content: at the end of the month to summarise transactions

options.label: D
options.content: before goods are supplied, often to request payment in advance

questions.stem: Goods listed at NLe 10,000 are sold with a 20% trade discount. What is the net invoice value?
questions.explanation:
Trade discount $= 20\% \times 10000 = 2000$. Invoice value $= 10000 - 2000 = $ NLe 8,000.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- NLe 2,000: That is the discount, not the invoice value.
- NLe 12,000: You added the discount instead of subtracting it.
- NLe 9,800: You subtracted 2% instead of 20%.

questions.stem: A retailer orders 40 cartons at a list price of NLe 250 each, less 20% trade discount, with 5% cash discount for payment within 14 days. How much does the retailer pay if paying promptly?
questions.explanation:
Gross $= 40 \times 250 = 10000$; less 20% $= 8000$; less 5% cash discount $= 8000 - 400 = $ NLe 7,600.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- NLe 8,000: That is the invoice value before cash discount.
- NLe 7,500: You added the two discounts (25%) and took them off the list price.
- NLe 9,500: You took only the 5% cash discount and forgot the trade discount.

questions.stem: The term E&OE on an invoice means
questions.explanation:
E&OE lets the seller correct mistakes in the invoice later.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- export and overseas exchange: This is not what the abbreviation stands for.
- ex-works or ex-warehouse: Ex-works is a different term.
- each order on exchange: This is not a trade term.

questions.stem: Goods cost 10,000 US dollars FOB. Freight to Freetown is 800 US dollars and insurance is 200 US dollars. What is the CIF price in US dollars?
questions.explanation:
CIF = cost + insurance + freight = 10,000 + 200 + 800 = 11,000 US dollars.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 10,800: You left out the insurance.
- 10,200: You left out the freight.
- 9,000: You subtracted freight and insurance instead of adding them.

questions.stem: Which document is a receipt for goods shipped, evidence of the contract of carriage and a document of title?
questions.explanation:
Whoever holds the bill of lading can claim the goods at the port of arrival.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- Air waybill: An air waybill is not a document of title.
- Certificate of origin: This shows where the goods were made.
- Consular invoice: This is certified by a consulate to check value.

questions.stem: An indent that allows the overseas agent to buy from any supplier who offers the best terms is
questions.explanation:
An open indent leaves the choice of supplier to the agent.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- a closed indent: A closed indent names the supplier or brand.
- a letter of credit: That is a bank's guarantee of payment.
- a shipping note: That gives the shipping company details of goods to be loaded.

papers.title: Transportation: practice set 1
papers.description: 8 original WASSCE-style objective questions on transportation, each with a worked solution and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: The main advantage of road transport over rail is that it
questions.explanation:
Lorries and vans deliver right to the buyer's premises, even in villages.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- is cheapest for very bulky goods over long distances: That is water or rail.
- is never affected by bad weather: Roads are badly affected by rain.
- has the fewest accidents: Road has more accidents than rail.

options.label: B
options.content: is cheapest for very bulky goods over long distances

options.label: C
options.content: is never affected by bad weather

questions.stem: Ships that sail on fixed routes to a fixed timetable at published rates are
questions.explanation:
Liners sail whether full or not; tramps go wherever there is cargo.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- tramps: Tramps have no fixed route or timetable.
- coasters: Coasters move goods between ports along one coast.
- tankers chartered for one voyage: Chartered ships go wherever they are hired to.

questions.stem: Which mode of transport is best for urgent, light and valuable goods such as medicines?
questions.explanation:
Air is the fastest mode, and its high cost is justified for urgent, light or valuable goods.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- Sea: Sea is slow, though cheap for bulk.
- Pipeline: Pipelines carry only liquids and gases.
- Rail: Rail suits heavy bulk over land.

questions.stem: A contract for the hire of a whole ship is a
questions.explanation:
A ship may be chartered for one voyage (voyage charter) or for a period (time charter).

**Why the other options are wrong**

- bill of lading: A bill of lading covers goods carried, not hire of the ship.
- waybill: A waybill lists goods carried by road or rail.
- ship's manifest: A manifest lists all cargo on board.

questions.stem: One advantage of containerisation is
questions.explanation:
Sealed containers are moved between modes without unpacking.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- no need for cranes at ports: Container ports need large cranes.
- more dock jobs: Containerisation reduces dock jobs.
- suitable for every kind of cargo: Some cargo, such as very large machinery, does not fit.

options.label: A
options.content: no need for cranes at ports

options.label: B
options.content: less handling, so less damage and theft

options.label: D
options.content: suitable for every kind of cargo

questions.stem: Transport removes the hindrance of
questions.explanation:
Transport moves goods from where they are produced to where they are wanted, creating place utility.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- time: Warehousing removes the hindrance of time.
- risk: Insurance removes the hindrance of risk.
- finance: Banking removes the hindrance of finance.

questions.stem: A haulier charges NLe 2 per tonne-kilometre plus NLe 500 for loading. What is the cost of carrying 20 tonnes of rice 300 km?
questions.explanation:
Tonne-km $= 20 \times 300 = 6000$; haulage $= 6000 \times 2 = 12000$; total $= 12000 + 500 = $ NLe 12,500.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- NLe 12,000: You left out the loading charge.
- NLe 6,500: You forgot to multiply by the rate of NLe 2.
- NLe 1,140: You added tonnes and kilometres instead of multiplying.

questions.stem: Which factor is MOST important when choosing transport for fresh fish?
questions.explanation:
Perishable goods must reach the market quickly, so speed comes first.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- The colour of the vehicle: Colour does not affect the choice.
- Whether the route is scenic: This does not matter for goods.
- The age of the driver: This is not a factor in choosing a mode.

options.label: D
options.content: Speed, because the goods are perishable

papers.title: Communication: practice set 1
papers.description: 8 original WASSCE-style objective questions on communication, each with a worked solution and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: In the communication process, the receiver's response to a message is called
questions.explanation:
Feedback tells the sender whether the message was understood.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- encoding: Encoding is the sender putting the idea into words or signals.
- noise: Noise is anything that distorts the message.
- the channel: The channel is the medium used.

questions.stem: A major advantage of written communication over oral communication is that it
questions.explanation:
Letters, memos and emails can be kept as evidence and checked later.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- gives immediate feedback: Oral communication gives quicker feedback.
- is always faster: Writing is usually slower.
- needs no literacy: Written messages need reading skills.

questions.stem: Poor network coverage that distorts a phone call is an example of
questions.explanation:
Noise is anything that interferes with the message on its way.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- feedback: Feedback is the receiver's response.
- decoding: Decoding is interpreting the message.
- encoding: Encoding is forming the message.

questions.stem: Which postal service gives compensation if an item is lost?
questions.explanation:
Registered mail is recorded at posting and signed for, with compensation for loss.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- Recorded delivery: Recorded delivery gives proof of posting and delivery, but little or no compensation.
- Poste restante: This holds mail for travellers to collect.
- Ordinary mail: Ordinary mail gives no compensation.

questions.stem: Compared with the post office, a courier service is usually
questions.explanation:
Couriers collect and deliver door to door with tracking, for a higher charge.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- cheaper and slower: Couriers are dearer and faster.
- run only by the government: Most couriers are private companies.
- unable to track parcels: Couriers usually offer full tracking.

options.label: A
options.content: faster and door to door, but more expensive

questions.stem: Communication from a manager to the staff is described as
questions.explanation:
Instructions passing down the organisation are downward communication.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- upward communication: Upward communication goes from staff to managers.
- horizontal communication: Horizontal communication is between people at the same level.
- external communication: External communication is with outsiders.

questions.stem: In Sierra Leone, the telecommunications sector is licensed and regulated by
questions.explanation:
NATCOM licenses and regulates mobile networks and other telecom operators.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- SALPOST: SALPOST provides postal services.
- the National Revenue Authority: The NRA collects taxes.
- the Sierra Leone Ports and Harbours Authority: This runs the ports.

options.label: D
options.content: the Sierra Leone Ports and Harbours Authority

questions.stem: A trader who cannot read is best reached by
questions.explanation:
Illiteracy is a barrier to written messages; radio, phone calls and pictures overcome it.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- long written reports: Written reports need literacy.
- email newsletters: Email needs reading skills.
- printed catalogues with no pictures: Text without pictures needs literacy.

papers.title: Warehousing: practice set 1
papers.description: 8 original WASSCE-style objective questions on warehousing, each with a worked solution and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: Warehousing removes the hindrance of
questions.explanation:
Warehouses hold goods from production until consumption, creating time utility.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- place: Transport removes the hindrance of place.
- risk: Insurance removes the hindrance of risk.
- ignorance: Advertising removes the hindrance of ignorance.

questions.stem: A warehouse where imported goods are kept until import duty is paid is a
questions.explanation:
Bonded warehouses are under customs control; duty is paid only when goods are released for home use.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- cold store: A cold store keeps perishables cool.
- private warehouse: A private warehouse holds the owner's own goods, duty paid.
- cooperative warehouse: This is shared by members of a cooperative.

questions.stem: An advantage of a bonded warehouse to the importer is that
questions.explanation:
The importer pays duty in instalments, batch by batch, and none on re-exports.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- no duty is ever paid on goods sold at home: Duty must be paid before release for home use.
- customs officers cannot inspect the goods: The goods are under customs control.
- goods cannot be repacked: Goods may be sampled, repacked or blended in bond.

options.label: A
options.content: no duty is ever paid on goods sold at home

options.label: B
options.content: customs officers cannot inspect the goods

options.label: C
options.content: duty is paid only on the goods taken out

questions.stem: Which warehouse document is a document of title that can be pledged to a bank as security?
questions.explanation:
A warehouse warrant can be transferred by endorsement and used as collateral.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- Warehouse keeper's receipt: This is only a receipt; it is not transferable.
- Goods received note: This only records goods arriving.
- Bin card: A bin card is a stock record.

questions.stem: Issuing older stock before newer stock is called
questions.explanation:
FIFO stops goods expiring or deteriorating on the shelves.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- last in, first out: That issues newest stock first.
- reorder level: Reorder level is the stock level that triggers a new order.
- buffer stock: Buffer stock is a safety reserve.

questions.stem: A wholesaler sells 40 cartons a day. Delivery takes 5 days and a buffer stock of 100 cartons is kept. What is the reorder level?
questions.explanation:
Reorder level = daily use × lead time + buffer stock = 40 × 5 + 100 = 300 cartons.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- 200 cartons: You left out the buffer stock.
- 145 cartons: You added the daily sales and the lead time instead of multiplying them.
- 100 cartons: That is only the buffer stock.

questions.stem: A trader buys 200 bags of rice at NLe 400 each, stores them for 4 months at NLe 15 per bag per month, and sells them at NLe 500 each. What is the profit?
questions.explanation:
Revenue $= 200 \times 500 = 100000$; cost $= 200 \times 400 + 200 \times 15 \times 4 = 92000$; profit $= $ NLe 8,000.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- NLe 20,000: You forgot the storage cost.
- NLe 17,000: You charged storage for one month only.
- NLe 12,000: That is the storage cost.

questions.stem: Which is a feature of a good warehouse?
questions.explanation:
A good warehouse is well located, secure, dry, fire-protected and well recorded.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- No fire protection, to save money: Fire protection is essential.
- Damp storage rooms: Goods must be kept dry.
- No records of goods received: Proper records are essential.

options.label: A
options.content: No fire protection, to save money

papers.title: Marketing and Advertising: practice set 1
papers.description: 8 original WASSCE-style objective questions on marketing and advertising, each with a worked solution and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: The marketing concept states that a firm should
questions.explanation:
Marketing starts with the customer's wants, not with the product.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- produce goods cheaply and wait for buyers: That is the production concept.
- push whatever it makes with strong selling: That is the selling concept.
- advertise only on television: This is not a concept of marketing.

options.label: A
options.content: produce goods cheaply and wait for buyers

options.label: B
options.content: push whatever it makes with strong selling

options.label: C
options.content: find out what customers want and produce to satisfy them

questions.stem: The four Ps of the marketing mix are product, price, place and
questions.explanation:
Product, price, place and promotion must fit together to suit the target customer.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- production: Production is not one of the four Ps.
- profit: Profit is a goal, not a P of the mix.
- packaging: Packaging is part of the product.

questions.stem: At which stage of the product life cycle does competition become strongest and sales level off?
questions.explanation:
At maturity most buyers already have the product, so firms compete hard for market share.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- Introduction: At introduction sales are low and competition weak.
- Growth: In growth, sales are still rising fast.
- Decline: In decline, sales fall and many competitors leave.

questions.stem: Advertising by a group of producers to promote a type of product rather than a brand is
questions.explanation:
For example, rice growers advertising 'Eat more local rice'.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- competitive advertising: Competitive advertising compares one brand with rivals.
- informative advertising: Informative advertising gives facts about a product.
- institutional advertising: Institutional advertising builds a firm's image.

questions.stem: Setting a low price for a new product to win market share quickly is
questions.explanation:
Penetration pricing attracts buyers away from rivals; the price may rise later.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- price skimming: Skimming starts high and lowers the price later.
- cost-plus pricing: Cost-plus adds a mark-up to cost.
- psychological pricing: Psychological pricing uses prices such as NLe 9.99.

questions.stem: A radio advert costs NLe 900 and reaches 300,000 listeners. What is the cost per thousand listeners?
questions.explanation:
300,000 listeners = 300 thousands. Cost per thousand $= 900 \div 300 = $ NLe 3.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- NLe 0.003: You divided by the number of listeners, not by thousands of listeners.
- NLe 333: You divided the listeners by the cost.
- NLe 300: You divided by 3 instead of by 300 thousands.

questions.stem: Free samples, discounts and competitions are examples of
questions.explanation:
Sales promotion gives short-term incentives to buy now.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- public relations: PR builds goodwill and the firm's image.
- personal selling: Personal selling is face-to-face selling by representatives.
- market research: Market research gathers information about customers.

questions.stem: Which is a disadvantage of advertising?
questions.explanation:
Advertising can exaggerate, persuade people to buy what they do not need and add to costs.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- It informs consumers about new products: That is an advantage.
- It helps firms produce on a large scale: That is an advantage.
- It funds radio and newspapers: That is an advantage.

options.label: A
options.content: It may mislead consumers with false claims

options.label: B
options.content: It informs consumers about new products

options.label: C
options.content: It helps firms produce on a large scale

papers.title: Banking: practice set 1
papers.description: 8 original WASSCE-style objective questions on banking, each with a worked solution and the reason behind every wrong option. Written by WASSCE Tutor, not taken from WAEC papers.

questions.stem: Which is a function of the central bank but NOT of commercial banks?
questions.explanation:
Only the central bank (the Bank of Sierra Leone) issues notes and coins.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- Accepting deposits from the public: Commercial banks do this.
- Granting loans and overdrafts to traders: Commercial banks do this.
- Providing safe deposit boxes: Commercial banks do this.

options.label: C
options.content: Granting loans and overdrafts to traders

questions.stem: The central bank acting as the lender of last resort means it
questions.explanation:
When commercial banks run short of funds, the central bank lends to them to prevent a crisis.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- lends to any trader who is refused by other banks: It does not lend to the public.
- is the last bank to open each day: This is not its meaning.
- pays the government's last debts: This is not its meaning.

options.label: A
options.content: lends to any trader who is refused by other banks

options.label: B
options.content: is the last bank to open each day

options.label: C
options.content: lends to commercial banks in difficulty

questions.stem: An account that gives the holder a cheque book and may allow an overdraft is a
questions.explanation:
Current accounts suit business payments; they usually pay no interest.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- savings account: Savings accounts usually have no cheque book.
- fixed deposit account: Fixed deposits are locked for a period.
- loan account: A loan account records money borrowed.

questions.stem: A trader overdraws an average of NLe 8,000 for 3 months at 24% a year. What is the interest?
questions.explanation:
$I = \dfrac{P \times R \times T}{100} = \dfrac{8000 \times 24 \times 3}{100 \times 12} = $ NLe 480.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- NLe 1,920: You charged a full year's interest.
- NLe 5,760: You multiplied by 3 years instead of 3 months.
- NLe 160: That is one month's interest; the overdraft lasted three months.

questions.stem: The bank on which a cheque is drawn is the
questions.explanation:
The three parties are the drawer (signs), the drawee (bank) and the payee (receives).

**Why the other options are wrong**

- drawer: The drawer is the account holder who signs the cheque.
- payee: The payee receives the money.
- endorsee: An endorsee receives a cheque by endorsement.

questions.stem: A cheque presented for payment more than six months after its date is
questions.explanation:
Banks refuse to pay stale cheques without the drawer's confirmation.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- a post-dated cheque: A post-dated cheque bears a future date.
- a crossed cheque: A crossed cheque must be paid into an account.
- a bearer cheque: A bearer cheque is payable to whoever holds it.

questions.stem: A cheque with two parallel lines drawn across it
questions.explanation:
A general crossing protects against theft because the money can be traced through an account.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- can be cashed over the counter by anyone: That is an open cheque.
- is payable only after six months: Crossing has nothing to do with dates.
- has been dishonoured: Crossing does not mean dishonour.

options.label: A
options.content: can be cashed over the counter by anyone

options.label: B
options.content: is payable only after six months

options.label: C
options.content: must be paid into a bank account

questions.stem: An instruction to a bank to pay a FIXED sum to a named payee at regular intervals is a
questions.explanation:
Standing orders suit fixed payments such as rent and loan repayments.

**Why the other options are wrong**

- direct debit: A direct debit lets the payee collect varying sums.
- bank draft: A bank draft is a cheque drawn by a bank on itself.
- credit transfer: A credit transfer pays several people with one slip.
